prompts.text: What's the easiest way for a new person to feel included in a group conversation?
Start a gathering with introductions or let people get to know each other naturally?
Tell us about joining a group where somebody made an effort to learn your name.
One person at a table hasn't spoken for a while. How would you bring them into the conversation without putting them on the spot?
A shared interest helps strangers connect even when their backgrounds differ.
Remembering a detail from someone's introduction is better than asking a dozen questions.
What kind of question gets everyone talking without turning into an interview?
Recall an occasion when an unexpected guest improved a group gathering.
Two people at an event know nobody else. What could the host do to help them meet?
Which group activity has helped you make a lasting friendship?
What's the best way to tell when a group is ready to change the subject?
Finish one discussion properly or let conversations wander into new topics?
Describe a group conversation that changed your perspective on something ordinary.
Three people start telling stories at the same time. How would you help everyone get a turn?
A lively conversation and a welcoming conversation are not always the same thing.
The person who listens carefully contributes as much as the person who speaks most.
Which topic brings out opinions you didn't know your friends held?
Tell us about a question someone asked that made the whole table go quiet and think.
A friend is interrupted repeatedly during a story. How would you make space for them to finish?
A long discussion about one big idea or a quick round of different questions?
What makes a group friendship last when people move to different cities?
Recall the first group chat you joined that became an important part of your routine.
An occasional group video call or short updates throughout the month?
One friend rarely responds online but always attends in-person gatherings. How should the group interpret it?
Friendship groups often develop unspoken expectations about response times.
A group chat should leave room for people who prefer less screen time.
Which group chat habit makes it easier to follow a conversation later?
Tell us about an online conversation that led to a memorable real-world meeting.
Friends living in different time zones want to catch up. What's a considerate way to choose a time?
What's one reason you'd rather call friends than send a message?
What does it mean for everyone to contribute fairly to a shared plan?
Decide where to go by voting or let each person choose an outing in turn?
Describe a trip where the best idea came from somebody who rarely plans.
Five friends have different budgets for an evening out. How should the group agree on a venue?
People who enjoy organising aren't always the ones who want to make every decision.
Checking everyone's budget early makes a group plan more comfortable.
Which part of planning an outing do you enjoy handling?
Tell us about a group plan that changed at the last moment for the better.
Everyone agrees to meet, but one person keeps arriving late. What would be a respectful approach?
Share a detailed itinerary or agree on one meeting point and decide the rest later?
What's a sign that someone in a group feels comfortable being themselves?
Tell us about a friend who helped you speak more freely among new people.
Play a lighthearted game first or begin with relaxed conversation?
Someone makes a joke that seems to upset another person. What should the group do next?
The same joke lands differently depending on the relationship between the people involved.
An apology matters more than winning an argument over whether a joke was funny.
What kind of teasing feels friendly to you, and what crosses the line?
Recall a time your group laughed about a misunderstanding after clearing it up.
A friend tells everyone they're uncomfortable with a recurring joke. How should the others respond?
Which group tradition is funny because nobody remembers how it started?
What's one small habit that makes someone a dependable friend?
A friend who checks in regularly or one who shows up whenever you need practical help?
Describe an ordinary favour you still remember years later.
Two people offer help to a friend but have different ideas about what to do. How should they coordinate?
People tend to notice different needs when the same friend is having a difficult week.
Asking permission before sharing someone's personal news is essential to friendship.
What helps a group support someone without making them feel watched?
Tell us about a time your friends quietly adjusted plans to accommodate somebody.
One person has had disappointing news and doesn't want the gathering to revolve around it. How would you respect that?
Send a collective message of support or let close friends reach out individually?
What would convince you to join a community outside your usual circle?
Tell us about a club or organisation where you met people with unexpected interests.
Join a weekend volunteer group or a regular class with new faces?
A group wants to welcome newcomers but already has plenty of inside jokes. What's a thoughtful first step?
Sharing the history of an inside joke helps newcomers join in without feeling excluded.
A group grows stronger when new people feel free to bring different ideas.
Which interest would you like to share with people outside your age group?
Recall learning an unfamiliar skill alongside people you had only just met.
Someone proposes an activity nobody has tried. What makes the risk worth taking?
What's a comfortable way to leave a social gathering when your energy is low?
How do you decide which opinions to share in a mixed group?
Talk through a disagreement together or leave it for a one-to-one conversation?
Describe a time you changed your view after hearing a friend's experience.
Two people disagree strongly about a film while everyone else wants to move on. What would you suggest?
People sometimes argue over definitions when they agree about the larger idea.
Disagreeing politely is more useful than pretending everyone thinks alike.
What's a question you ask to understand an opinion before responding to it?
Tell us about a debate that ended with everyone learning something new.
A friend feels embarrassed after sharing an unpopular view. How should the group keep the discussion respectful?
Hear everyone's view in turn or let the discussion develop without a formal order?
Who in your circle is best at remembering important dates?
Recall a small surprise from friends that mattered more than an elaborate celebration.
Plan a group birthday outing or make a collection of personal notes for the person?
A friend dislikes being the centre of attention but the group wants to celebrate them. What should guide the plan?
Celebrating friends well begins with knowing whether they enjoy surprises.
A sincere message from several friends beats a party the guest of honour doesn't enjoy.
What kind of achievement deserves more recognition among friends?
Tell us about a gathering where someone else's success made the whole group happy.
A friend finishes a long personal project and asks for a low-key celebration. What would you organise?
Which shared accomplishment has made you feel closer to a group?
What's an experience you'd like your friends to try together once?
Start an informal book exchange or take turns sharing a favourite song?
Tell us about a group activity that became an unexpected tradition.
A friend proposes a monthly gathering, but schedules keep clashing. How might the group make it practical?
Friendship traditions often evolve when everyone's responsibilities change.
Keeping a group connected depends more on consistency than on expensive outings.
Which small group tradition would still feel meaningful after several years?
Recall saying goodbye at a gathering when you knew you wouldn't see everyone for a while.
Friends from different stages of life meet at one table. What would help them connect?
End a gathering with a group photograph or with everyone suggesting the next activity?
